item.text: {"search_note":"I did not find reliable 2024 evidence of a nationwide internet shutdown in the DRC under Tshisekedi. I also did not find strong direct evidence of sophisticated technical surveillance or spyware deployment in the 2024 material I checked. The evidence that does exist is mostly about arrests, prosecutions, media closures, incommunicado detention, and legal pressure on journalists and activists, which still squarely fits 4B.9 as a negative record.","evidence":[{"title":"DR Congo’s arrest of activists invokes déjà vu of growing repression","publisher":"Amnesty International","date":"2024-02-16","url":"https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/02/dr-congos-arrest-of-activists-invokes-deja-vu-of-growing-repression/","summary":"Security services arrested LUCHA activists in Kinshasa in an abduction-like manner, held some in unknown detention, and forced others to flee. This is direct evidence of administrative harassment and coercive suppression of dissent.","question_ids":["4B.9","4B.6","4B.7","4B.3"]},{"title":"DRC: AUTHORITIES MUST IMMEDIATELY FREE DETAINED JOURNALIST","publisher":"Amnesty International","date":"2024-03-08","url":"https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/03/drc-authorities-must-immediately-free-detained-journalist/","summary":"Amnesty said Stanis Bujakera’s detention was “judicial harassment” meant to chill criticism and “all free voices.” This is strong evidence of state pressure on independent reporting.","question_ids":["4B.9","4B.6","4B.3"]},{"title":"DR Congo: Human rights agenda for Tshisekedi’s second term","publisher":"Human Rights Watch","date":"2024-03-06","url":"https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/03/06/human-rights-agenda-democratic-republic-congo","summary":"HRW said the government had increasingly cracked down online on journalists, activists, critics, and opposition members, and urged reform of the Digital Code because it criminalized sharing “false news.” This supports a finding of digital/legal controls used to restrict political freedom.","question_ids":["4B.9","4B.6","4B.3"]},{"title":"East and Southern Africa: Journalists targeted amid ongoing crackdown on media","publisher":"Amnesty International","date":"2024-05-03","url":"https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/05/media-freedom-under-threat/","summary":"Amnesty reported that Congolese authorities closed down a dozen media outlets and programs on charges like “spreading false rumors,” “inciting revolt,” and defamation, and continued to attack press freedom. This is direct evidence of censorship-like administrative pressure.","question_ids":["4B.9","4B.6"]},{"title":"2024 Country Reports on Human Rights Practices: Democratic Republic of the Congo","publisher":"U.S. Department of State via ECOI","date":"2024","url":"https://www.ecoi.net/en/document/2128488.html","summary":"The report says security officials routinely held activists, protesters, journalists, and opposition members incommunicado, including in unofficial detention centers run by intelligence and guard services. That is strong evidence of coercive administrative control used against political activity.","question_ids":["4B.9","4B.3","4B.6","4B.7"]},{"title":"Freedom in the World 2024: Democratic Republic of Congo","publisher":"Freedom House","date":"2024","url":"https://freedomhouse.org/country/democratic-republic-congo/freedom-world/2024","summary":"Freedom House noted that many Congolese still openly discuss corruption and insecurity on social media, which is a limited sign that the state did not impose a total information blackout. This is weak counterevidence only, not proof of protection.","question_ids":["4B.9","4B.6"]}]}
